name: Close-Grip Push-Up
description: The close-grip push-up is a push-up variation where the hands are placed directly beneath the shoulders or slightly closer together than a standard push-up. The reduced hand spacing shifts the mechanical advantage toward the triceps brachii while maintaining significant pectoral involvement. It is easier than the diamond push-up but more tricep-focused than the standard push-up.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a plank position with hands placed directly beneath or slightly inside the shoulders. Fingers point forward. Body forms a straight line from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Use a mat for wrist comfort if needed.
steps: Step 1: Position hands shoulder-width or slightly narrower, directly under or slightly inside the shoulders.
Step 2: Hold a rigid plank body position with core engaged.
Step 3: Inhale and lower the chest toward the hands by bending the elbows, which track close to the sides of the torso.
Step 4: Pause at the bottom, then exhale and press back to the top.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent; exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, which shifts the exercise back to a standard push-up
safety_considerations: If wrist discomfort occurs, use push-up handles or rotate hands slightly outward
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from near chest-to-floor to full arm extension.
coaching_cues: Keep the elbows tracking along the sides of the torso like train tracks
